verses.text: After Abimelech, Tola the son of Puah, the son of Dodo, a man of Issachar, arose to save Israel. He lived in Shamir in the hill country of Ephraim.
He judged Israel twenty-three years, and died, and was buried in Shamir.
After him Jair, the Gileadite arose, and he judged Israel twenty-two years.
He had thirty sons who rode on thirty donkey colts, and they had thirty cities, which are called Havvoth Jair to this day, which are in the land of Gilead.
Jair died, and was buried in Kamon.

The children of Israel again did that which was evil in Yahweh’s sight, and served the Baals, the Ashtaroth, the gods of Syria, the gods of Sidon, the gods of Moab, the gods of the children of Ammon, and the gods of the Philistines. They abandoned Yahweh, and didn’t serve him.
Yahweh’s anger burned against Israel, and he sold them into the hand of the Philistines, and into the hand of the children of Ammon.

They troubled and oppressed the children of Israel that year. For eighteen years, they oppressed all the children of Israel that were beyond the Jordan in the land of the Amorites, which is in Gilead.
The children of Ammon passed over the Jordan to fight also against Judah, and against Benjamin, and against the house of Ephraim, so that Israel was very distressed.
The children of Israel cried to Yahweh, saying, “We have sinned against you, even because we have forsaken our God, and have served the Baals.”
Yahweh said to the children of Israel, “Didn’t I save you from the Egyptians, and from the Amorites, from the children of Ammon, and from the Philistines?
The Sidonians also, and the Amalekites, and the Maonites, oppressed you; and you cried to me, and I saved you out of their hand.
Yet you have forsaken me, and served other gods. Therefore I will save you no more.
Go and cry to the gods which you have chosen. Let them save you in the time of your distress!”
The children of Israel said to Yahweh, “We have sinned! Do you to us whatever seems good to you; only deliver us, please, today.”
They put away the foreign gods from among them, and served Yahweh; and his soul was grieved for the misery of Israel.
Then the children of Ammon were gathered together and encamped in Gilead. The children of Israel assembled themselves together and encamped in Mizpah.
The people, the princes of Gilead, said to one another, “Who is the man who will begin to fight against the children of Ammon? He shall be head over all the inhabitants of Gilead.”

footnotes.content: After the chaos of Abimelech, Tola stepped in quietly—a man from Issachar, a region known for understanding the times. He wasn't flashy or famous, but he arose to save Israel. Sometimes the Lord sends the steady hand we don't notice until later, when we look back and see how much quieter things became.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Twenty-three years Tola judged—a long, uncelebrated tenure. No miracles, no fame, just faithful work. There's grace in the unglamorous judges, in the long obedience in the same direction. Tola reminds us that stability and faithfulness often pass unnoticed while we're looking for the dramatic.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jair the Gileadite came next, and for twenty-two years, the cycle continued. Gilead was east of the Jordan—a place of refuge and strength in later stories. The Lord keeps raising up leaders, even when His people refuse to learn. His faithfulness outlasts our forgetfulness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Thirty sons riding thirty colts, thirty cities in the land of Gilead—a marker of prosperity and clan strength. The very names Havvoth Jair (villages of Jair) remain to Judges' day, a monument to his influence. Power and resources are real, but they won't protect us from the consequences of turning away from the Lord.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jair died and was buried in Kamon—another good judge laid to rest. Yet notice: prosperity, status, thirty sons, and thirty cities could not change the direction of Israel's heart. What a sober thought: influence and success in human terms cannot substitute for keeping covenant with God.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Again Israel did evil, and this time their idolatry sprawls across the map—Baals, Ashtaroth, the gods of Syria, Sidon, Moab, Ammon, the Philistines. It's overwhelming, almost absurd in its reach. They didn't just stray; they drank deep from every false well around them. The heart that leaves God fills itself with everything else.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh's anger burned. He didn't scold from a distance—He acted. He sold them into the hands of the Philistines and Ammonites, allowing the consequences their choices invited. A hard mercy: He let them taste what separation from Him actually cost.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Eighteen years of oppression. Long enough that a generation grew up knowing only humiliation and the weight of enemy rule east of the Jordan, in the land of the Amorites. The Scripture doesn't rush through the suffering—it lingers, so we feel how long it was, how deep it bit.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Ammonites crossed the Jordan to raid Judah, Benjamin, and Ephraim too. The oppression wasn't confined to the east—it spread and deepened until all Israel was very distressed. When we turn from God, our troubles compound; they don't stay neat or local.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: At last—Israel cried out. "We have sinned, we have forsaken our God." There's something true in their confession, though it may still be thin. Yet the Lord hears the cry even before the heart is fully turned, because He desires to save. He was waiting for them to call.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh's answer came swift and pointed: "Didn't I save you from the Egyptians, the Amorites, the Ammonites, the Philistines?" He rehearsed His faithfulness like a Father reminding His child of all He'd done. Every deliverance He'd given became a witness against their ingratitude.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Sidonians, Amalekites, and Maonites—more enemies, more times He saved them. Yahweh's list was long, and His patience had been longer still. Every rescue they'd forgotten was another proof that His nature is to deliver those who call.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Yet you have forsaken me, and served other gods. Therefore I will save you no more." The words landed hard. This wasn't a tantrum—it was a statement of covenant reality: He cannot save those who refuse to turn. The line is real, though it invites them to cross back.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Go and cry to the gods which you have chosen." A mirror held up: let your false gods prove themselves in your distress. There's searing mercy in this challenge—He was calling them to wake up and see the lie they'd believed. The gods cannot save.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo of this cry in their own deepest moments: "We have sinned! Do with us whatever seems good to you; only deliver us, please, today." The words are simple—almost desperate—but that's where real repentance lives. When we stop negotiating and simply ask to be delivered, the Lord draws near.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They put away the foreign gods. Not perfectly, not forever—but they acted. And Yahweh's soul was grieved for the misery of Israel. Picture it: He felt their pain. His anger had a purpose—to bring them to this moment of humble obedience, so He could move toward them in compassion.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Ammonites gathered in Gilead; Israel assembled at Mizpah. The battle lines were drawn, and a deliverer would soon emerge from the people themselves. The stage was set, and their repentance opened the door for Him to act.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Who is the man who will begin to fight? He shall be head over all." The promise hung in the air—leadership and honor for the one who will lead them forward. The people were ready, the enemy was near, and Israel's cry for a savior was about to be answered. The Lord works through our willingness and our desperation.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
